h1: The 6 Best Lawn Mowers Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $200 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six lawn mowers under $200, covering cordless, gas, corded and reel types, with who each suits and the tradeoffs to expect.
summary: The Litheli 14-inch cordless is the best lawn mower under $200: a brushless motor, 5.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and no fuel or cord. The PowerSmart EasyCut is the pick for a wider 18-inch gas cut, and the LawnMaster suits small yards near an outlet. The reel mower is the cheapest to run, the others suit tiny lawns.
intro: Under $200, the first decision is not deck width, it is how the mower gets its power. A wide deck is no help if you dread the pull cord, the fuel can or the extension lead, because the dread turns into a lawn that gets cut every second weekend instead of every week. The mower you will actually start beats the one with the better spec sheet.

We reviewed six mowers on paper and scored them on the Primea framework, comparing power type, deck size, height adjustment, upkeep and what lawn each suits. Scores draw on listed specs and owner comments, not our own mowing, and prices appear as buckets. Everything here costs under $200, so the compromises are visible.

products.name: Litheli 14-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower, 5.0Ah Battery
products.verdict: Brushless cordless convenience with a battery included.
products.description:
The Litheli is a 14-inch cordless mower with a brushless motor, a 5.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and five cutting heights, in the $50 to $100 bucket. A brushless motor has no carbon brushes to wear, so it runs cooler and draws less from the pack, which stretches a mowing session on a small battery.

It wins because it removes the three things budget mowers make you tolerate: cords, fuel and a missing battery. The PowerSmart cuts a wider swath, but it asks for oil and gas, and the LawnMaster tethers you to an outlet. Both cost more.

Buy it for a lawn up to about 3,000 square feet. The honest limit is the 14-inch deck plus one battery: a larger lawn means more passes and a pack that runs out partway, so a second battery becomes necessary.
products.idealFor: Small lawns up to about 3,000 square feet.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is larger than a small suburban plot.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyCut 18-Inch Gas Lawn Mower
products.verdict: The widest deck here, powered by gas.
products.description:
The PowerSmart EasyCut pairs an 18-inch deck with a 144cc 4-cycle gas engine, side discharge and five height positions, in the $100 to $200 bucket. It is the widest deck in the group, and a gas engine has no battery to drain halfway across the lawn.

It ranks second because width costs you simplicity. Four fewer inches of cut per pass sounds trivial, but over a half-acre it removes a lot of turns. Against that, you pay in oil changes, fuel, a pull start and noise that the Litheli avoids entirely.

Buy it for a small to mid-size yard where the cut width matters and you accept engine upkeep. Skip it if you do not want to handle fuel or oil, since a mower that is a chore to start ends up used less often than the lawn requires.
products.idealFor: Small to mid-size yards that need a wider cut.
products.skipIf: You do not want to handle fuel or oil.

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1114K 15-Inch Corded Electric Mower
products.verdict: Steady power with no battery to wear out.
products.description:
The LawnMaster MEB1114K is a corded electric with a 15-inch deck and an 11-amp motor, in the $100 to $200 bucket. The cord gives it constant power with no battery to age, so performance in the tenth season matches the first, and the motor never fades near the end of a charge.

It ranks third because the cord is a leash. The Litheli removes it for less money, and a cord snags on trees, beds and corners, forcing you to flip it over each turn. Its 15-inch deck is only marginally wider than the Litheli's 14 inch, a minor gain.

Buy it for a small, open yard near an outlet. Skip it if your yard has many trees or flower beds, where cord management turns mowing into a puzzle and you spend more time handling the lead than cutting.
products.idealFor: Small open yards close to an outlet.
products.skipIf: Your yard has many trees or beds.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: Zero fuel, zero cord, and the lowest running cost.
products.description:
The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 is a push reel mower with a 14-inch cutting width and a four-blade reel, in the $50 to $100 bucket. A reel scissors the grass against a fixed bar instead of whacking it, which is why it is quiet and needs no fuel, battery or cord.

It ranks fourth because you are the engine. On a small, flat lawn that stays trimmed, it is the cheapest to own and the gentlest on the neighborhood. Let the grass get tall or thick and the reel stalls, so it only works if you mow often.

Buy it for a small flat lawn where running cost and quiet matter most. Skip it if your grass grows tall, your lawn slopes, or you want a mower that handles a missed week, because the reel will push over taller stems instead of cutting them.
products.skipIf: Your grass gets tall or your lawn slopes.

products.name: 13-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower, 40V
products.verdict: Light and compact for tiny patches of lawn.
products.description:
The 13-inch cordless mower runs on a 40V battery platform and is built for weight and storage, in the $100 to $200 bucket. It has the narrowest deck here, and its small footprint lets it hang on a wall or fit in a closet.

It ranks fifth because the Litheli gives a wider deck, a listed brushless motor and a 5.0Ah battery for less money. That leaves this one with a compact, lightweight design as its argument, and the listing gives few details beyond that. A 40V platform could pay off if you buy other tools on it.

Buy it for a tiny patch of lawn, or as a backup mower for a second small area. Skip it if value per dollar is the goal, which is the Litheli's territory, or if you need a clear runtime figure before buying.
products.idealFor: Tiny lawn patches or backup mowing.
products.skipIf: You want the most features per dollar.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BESTA512CM 3-in-1 Mower, Weed Eater and Edger
products.verdict: A mower, trimmer and edger for very small yards.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER BESTA512CM is a corded 3-in-1 with a 12-inch cutting width and a 6.5-amp motor that works as a mower, trimmer and edger, in the $50 to $100 bucket. The idea is to replace three tools with one, which suits a shed with no space.

It ranks last because a 12-inch width and a small motor only fit a tiny yard. Against the LawnMaster's 11-amp motor and 15-inch deck, it gives up cutting power for versatility. It is also corded, which brings the same cord limits.

Buy it for patios, courtyards and edging strips along a path. Skip it if you have a normal-sized lawn, since a narrow deck means many passes, and the transition between mower and trimmer modes adds fiddling each time you switch.
products.idealFor: Very small yards, patios and edging jobs.
products.skipIf: You have a normal sized lawn.

whatMatters.detail: Cordless mowers run on a battery, corded ones plug in, gas ones burn fuel and reel mowers run on your own effort. Each changes cost, noise and upkeep. Pick the type you will actually use each week, because a mower you avoid starting leaves the lawn long. The Litheli is cordless, the LawnMaster corded, the PowerSmart gas and the American Lawn Mower a reel.

Amp-hours describe how much energy a battery stores, so a larger figure means more mowing per charge. The Litheli ships with a 5.0Ah battery and charger, which keeps the first-year cost down. Check that the battery and charger are both included in the listing, because a bare tool without them costs far more.

Wider decks cut more grass per pass but are heavier and harder to store. A 14-inch deck suits small lawns, and the 18-inch PowerSmart suits mid-size ones. Measure your lawn before choosing, and count the passes: a few extra minutes per mow matter less than a mower you resent hauling out of the shed.

Multiple cutting positions let you raise the deck in summer heat and lower it in spring. Cutting too short in hot weather stresses grass and invites weeds. The Litheli and PowerSmart both list five positions, a useful range. Look for the number of positions in the specs, and note whether adjustment is per wheel or a single lever.

Corded models need an outlet and careful routing around obstacles, while gas models need oil, fuel and annual care. Think about how much upkeep you accept before you buy. Read the listing for cord length or engine notes, and remember that the LawnMaster and BLACK+DECKER both depend on an extension cord reaching the far corner.

faq.q: Is a reel mower good enough?
faq.a: For small flat lawns kept short, yes. The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 is quiet and costs nothing to run, but it is hard work on tall or thick grass, so mow before the lawn gets away from you.
Buying too wide a deck for a tiny yard. The 18-inch PowerSmart adds weight and storage trouble when a 14-inch Litheli would finish the same small lawn in similar time and fit easily in a shed.

faq.q: Is the PowerSmart gas mower worth it?
faq.a: If you want an 18-inch deck and accept upkeep, yes. The Litheli is simpler for small lawns, and the PowerSmart makes sense once the lawn is big enough for the extra width to matter.

faq.q: Does the Litheli include a battery?
faq.a: Yes. The listing includes a 5.0Ah battery and charger, so it is ready to use out of the box. For a bigger lawn, plan to buy a second battery, since one pack limits runtime.

faq.q: How do I store a gas mower?
faq.a: Handle the fuel per the manual and keep the PowerSmart dry. Change the oil each season, and run the tank low or add a stabilizer before storing it for winter. Clean grass from the deck underside too.

faq.q: Can a corded mower cut a big lawn?
faq.a: Reach is limited by the cord, so a corded model such as the LawnMaster suits small yards only. For larger lawns choose the cordless Litheli or the gas PowerSmart, which have no tether.

finalTake: For most small lawns, the Litheli 14-inch is the best mower under $200: brushless, battery included and free of cords and fuel. The PowerSmart earns a place for a wider gas cut, and the LawnMaster suits yards near an outlet. The reel mower wins on running cost, while the 13-inch cordless and the 3-in-1 fit only tiny patches.
